title: Thonny REPL Workflow
description: An interactive vis-network flow diagram of the round trip of code and text between the Thonny editor, the Shell/REPL, and the Pico 2 board over USB serial.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Embedded Systems
Development Tools

learningObjectives: Explain the relationship between the editor pane, the Shell/REPL, and the board
Summarize why Run behaves differently from typing at the prompt
Identify the USB serial link as the return route for print() output
prerequisites: Thonny installed with a Pico 2 connected
A .py file holds Python source code

controls.label: Script Path
controls.purpose: Highlight the route a saved script takes and dim the direct-typing route

controls.label: Direct REPL
controls.purpose: Highlight the direct-typing route and dim the script route

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Restore all nodes and edges to their normal colors

controls.label: Any node
controls.purpose: Show a one-sentence definition of that term

assumptions: The USB link is presented as a single logical channel rather than a full serial protocol stack
limitations: Does not model soft reboots, paste mode, or the raw REPL protocol Thonny uses internally

keyQuestions: Which nodes appear on the script path but not the direct path?
Where does a print() statement actually execute?
commonMisconceptions: That the script runs on the laptop and results are sent to the board
That the Shell is a separate program from the board's interpreter
assessmentOpportunities: Explain where print(2+2) is evaluated and how the result reaches the screen
